# Year 9 History Lesson Plan: Causes of the First World War

**Fits NC unit**: *Challenges for Britain, Europe and the wider world, 1901–present* – "the First World War and the Peace Settlement"
**Prior knowledge assumed**: Basic chronology of early 20th century Europe (taught previous lesson)
**Class**: 34 students, mixed attainment, 6 with reading age <9

## Learning Objective
To identify and explain the MAIN causes of WWI (Militarism, Alliances, Imperialism, Nationalism) and how they combined to turn an assassination into a continental war.

**Success criteria (differentiated, shared verbally + on slide, not printed):**
- All students can name the four MAIN causes
- Most can explain each one in their own words with an example
- Some can explain how the causes *linked together* and why the assassination was a "trigger" rather than a root cause

---

## Timing Table

| Time | Activity | Teacher action | Student action |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0–5 min | **Starter (hook)** | Project question: *"Your two best mates promise to always fight for you if anyone starts on you. You promise the same for them. What could go wrong?"* Take 2–3 verbal answers. | Think–pair–share (30 sec think, 1 min pair), 2–3 hands up to share |
| 5–8 min | **Link to objective** | Explain: this is basically what European countries did in 1914 — called an "alliance." Reveal LO and MAIN acronym on slide. | Listen; table monitors collect pre-counted sheet piles (6 per table) |
| 8–23 min | **Modelled input** | Go through M-A-I-N one at a time using projector slide (map/images) while reading the matching box on the sheet *aloud*, so no one is blocked by text. Students underline/highlight the key word in each box as you go (colour cue matches slide). Use 1 quick check question per cause via **cold-call** (lolly sticks/name list) to sample understanding across ability range. | Follow along, highlight key terms, answer cold-call questions |
| 23–36 min | **Paired task** | Set two tasks on the sheet (Alliance diagram labelling + Sort-the-causes grid). Pair weaker readers with a stronger "talk partner" (pre-assigned in seating plan) — TA/LSA (if present) directed to the 6 lowest readers. Circulate, prompting with sentence starters. 10 min timer on screen. | Work in pairs, complete sheet tasks 1 & 2 |
| 36–41 min | **Mid-point feedback** | Cold-call 3–4 pairs to share one answer each; correct misconceptions live on slide (e.g. clarify Franz Ferdinand ≠ main cause, just the spark). | Check/correct own sheet |
| 41–44 min | **Independent exit task** | Direct students to Task 3 on sheet: one-sentence answer using given starter, differentiated by three starter stems (simple/medium/stretch, see sheet). | Write exit sentence in box on sheet |
| 44–50 min | **Plenary / AfL check** | Run rapid whole-class recall: hold up fingers 1–4 for each MAIN letter as teacher says the full word ("Militarism" = finger 1 etc. — instant visual check of recall). Then ask students to **traffic-light** their exit sentence box (green = confident, amber = unsure, red = need help) using pen they already have. Teacher scans room visually, addresses 1–2 common ambers aloud before bell. Collect sheets at door as exit pass. | Finger-recall; traffic-light own work; hand sheet in on way out |

---

## The Single A4 Sheet (printed double-sided, one per student)

**Design notes**: Arial/Comic Sans 14pt, short lines, lots of white space, icons next to each heading, colour-coded headers (match projector slides), boxes not paragraphs.

### Side 1 – "What caused World War One? MAIN"

| Letter | Picture icon | Key word (bold) | Plain-English box |
|---|---|---|---|
| **M** | soldier/gun icon | **Militarism** | Countries were building huge armies and navies. Everyone felt they had to be ready for war. |
| **A** | linked chain icon | **Alliances** | Countries made promises to help each other if attacked. This meant a small fight could drag in many countries. |
| **I** | globe/flag icon | **Imperialism** | Countries competed for colonies (land) around the world. This caused jealousy and tension. |
| **N** | flag icon | **Nationalism** | Extreme pride in your own country. Some groups wanted independence; some countries wanted to show they were the strongest. |

*Glossary strip along bottom with 4 key words + simple 4-word definitions + small picture each, for quick reference.*

### Side 2

- **Diagram**: Two boxes — "Triple Alliance" (Germany, Austria-Hungary, Italy) and "Triple Entente" (Britain, France, Russia) with simple arrows showing "promised to help."
- **Comic-strip style timeline** (4 small boxes, 1 sentence each): Assassination in Sarajevo → Austria-Hungary blames Serbia → Alliances pull in other countries → War begins, 1914.
- **Task 1**: Label the two alliance boxes with the correct countries (word bank given).
- **Task 2 — Sort the causes**: 8 short statement cards printed in a grid (e.g. "Germany built more battleships," "Serbia wanted independence from Austria-Hungary") — students write M/A/I/N next to each.
- **Task 3 — Exit sentence** (three tiered starters, student picks one):
  - *Simple*: "One cause of WWI was ___ because ___."
  - *Medium*: "The MAIN cause I think was most important is ___ because ___."
  - *Stretch*: "The assassination was only the trigger because ___."
- Small traffic-light box (⬤⬤⬤) for self-assessment at the end.

---

## Differentiation Summary
- **Low readers (6 students)**: all text read aloud as sheet is used; icons/colour coding reduce reliance on decoding; paired with stronger talk partner; sentence starters remove the writing barrier; TA (if available) directed here.
- **Core**: sorting/labelling task builds from direct teaching, cold-call ensures accountability.
- **Higher attainers**: stretch sentence starter pushes into analysis (trigger vs. underlying cause); can be asked verbally "which cause do you think mattered most and why?" during feedback.

## Checking Understanding Before the Bell
Three low-cost, no-printing methods layered in the final 6 minutes:
1. **Finger-recall quiz** – instant whole-class check of factual recall (no materials needed).
2. **Traffic-light self-assessment** on the exit sentence already written on the sheet.
3. **Visual scan + verbal correction** – teacher walks the room in the last 2 minutes, spots ambers/reds, clarifies live before students leave; sheets collected as an exit pass for the teacher to review that evening and inform next lesson's starter.
